operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table/column names: 'Act','Scene','CharName','Abbrev','ParagraphNum','PlainText','LongTitle','GenreType','work_id','chapter_id','character_id' — must be double-quoted verbatim.
Column named 'Date' (works.Date) is INTEGER storing years (1589..1607), not a date string; declared type INTEGER so TS dispatches to Number, not Date fuzzer.
Column named 'Description' exists in BOTH chapters and characters with different value distributions (519 vs 467 distinct) — literal pool keyed by (table,col) must not merge them.

Column named 'id' is PK in all 4 tables; literal pool for (t,'id') will be polluted across tables via FK-root ancestor mapping (works.id is root of chapters.work_id, chapters.id root of paragraphs.chapter_id).
chapters.id and paragraphs.chapter_id share the SAME sample values (18704..18708) — FK values are drawn from parent's final column, so chapter_id must come from chapters.id after PK dedup.
paragraphs.chapter_id has 'default 0 not null' — default is irrelevant to TS (it always supplies a value) but NOT NULL means failed inserts are silently dropped.

paragraphs.id samples are large (630863+) while chapters.id are 18704+ — autoincrement sequences differ; TS Number fuzzer will generate small ints (scale from 'INTEGER' -> no args -> scale 0, range [-1,1]) that collide with PK dedup.
works has only 43 rows; chapters.work_id distinct=43 (full coverage); paragraphs.character_id distinct=1219 < characters 1266 (some characters unreferenced).
characters.CharName and Abbrev have nearly identical distinct counts (957 vs 964) and identical first samples — likely near-duplicate columns; TS String fuzzer treats them independently.
characters.Description contains empty string '' as a sample — String fuzzer's length range [0,20] and contaminate can produce ''; fine.
PlainText samples contain newlines ('\n') and truncated text ('[Enter DUKE ORSINO, CURIO, and other Lor') — String fuzzer CHARSET has no newline, so fresh values differ in shape from originals.
No composite keys, no self-FKs, no dangling FKs, no non-unique parents, no storage-class/declared-type contradictions (all INTEGER->integer, TEXT->text).
operator_ts_expectations: All id/Act/Scene/ParagraphNum/work_id/chapter_id/character_id/Date columns -> Number fuzzer with scale=0 (INTEGER has no args), range [-1,1], int perturbation +-1/+-2; produces tiny ints unlike originals (Act 1-5, Scene 1-155, Date 1589-1607).

works.Date (INTEGER, values 1589-1607) gets Number fuzzer -> values in {-2..2} roughly; any query filtering Date BETWEEN 1590 AND 1610 returns empty on generated instances -> likely FN driver (implausible values).

Act/Scene/ParagraphNum small-range ints: Number fuzzer's list range [min(el), max(el)+1] overwritten to full range [-1,1] (upstream quirk) -> generated Act values mostly -1,0,1,2; queries 'Act = 3' or 'Scene > 10' miss -> FN.

TEXT columns (Title, LongTitle, CharName, Abbrev, Description, PlainText, GenreType) -> String fuzzer, length range from min/max of 5 sampled originals + pool; fresh strings over 'a-zA-Z 0-9()' with 50% contaminate -> implausible names, no real Shakespeare titles -> FN on LIKE '%Night%' style.

GenreType has only 5 distinct values (Comedy/Tragedy/History/Poem/Sonnet); String fuzzer with p=0.2 mostly fresh strings -> 'GenreType = Comedy' rarely matches -> FN; ENUM-like column not respected by TS.

FK columns (work_id, chapter_id, character_id) drawn from parent's FINAL filtered column with replacement -> duplicates in child FK values; joins produce many-to-many fan-out unlike original 1:many -> FP on COUNT/aggregate queries.
PK dedup (sample_fresh_primary_keys) drops duplicate id rows; with Number fuzzer producing few distinct small ints, many rows dropped -> small tables, empty results for queries expecting rows -> FN.

works has 43 rows; choose_table_sizes may give it 1+30*u (~1-31) or 30+int(u*200) rows; if smaller than chapters, FK fan-out from chapters.work_id to works.id still works but join cardinality differs.
characters.CharName vs Abbrev near-duplicate: TS generates independent strings -> queries comparing CharName=Abbrev (if any) behave differently -> potential FP/FN.
PlainText newlines absent from CHARSET -> queries with LIKE '%\n%' or length(PlainText) thresholds miss -> FN.
No Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers dispatched (no such declared types) — Date fuzzer template logic not exercised on this DB.
Empty-string Description sample: String fuzzer may emit '' matching original empty rows -> some queries on Description='' may accidentally match -> possible FP.
